title: Microedge prefetch velocity briefing
summary: Quick internal benchmark notebook exploring how aggressive prefetching at edge nodes (microedge) affects P50/P90/P99 latency and $/1k request under microburst traffic. Focus on prefetch velocity vs waste (extra tokens fetched) tradeoffs.
body:
Purpose:
Assess prefetch velocity (how many tokens/context we proactively fetch into KV cache at session start and during short bursts) on edge nodes. Goal: quantify latency benefit vs incremental token cost and propose a small heuristic for the console to recommend prefetch settings per route.

Background / context:
- Microedge: lightweight edge pool (N1 instances) used for low-latency interactive workloads in region.
- Prefetch velocity: rate and amount we request to warm KV/prefix caches before incoming user turns. Higher velocity -> higher hit rate early in session but more wasted compute for abandoned sessions.
- This is a console/optimize feature: we want to suggest defaults per-route.

Bench configuration (toy but repeatable):
- Model: small-ish Llama-2 style open model shim (simulated kernels) to avoid licensing; uses same kernel mix as production for latency shape.
- Node type: edge-small (1 GPU equiv), simulates microedge latency 4–7ms base.
- Session length distribution: 70% 1–3 turns, 20% 4–8, 10% >9 turns (empirical from Prod-sampled cohort 2028-05).
- Burst profile: Poisson spikes with 5s half-life; peak concurrency up to 120 QPS.
- Metrics: P50/P90/P99 server-side generation latency (ms), KV cache hit-rate (per-token), additional tokens fetched per-session (waste), estimated $/1k requests (token cost) assuming $0.000012/token.

Quick results (aggregated):
- Baseline (no prefetch): P50 18ms, P90 46ms, P99 210ms, KV hit 12%, extra tokens 0, cost $/1k = 0.86
- Soft prefetch (first 32 tokens at 1x velocity): P50 13ms, P90 36ms, P99 160ms, KV hit 28%, extra tokens 32*session_warm_frac ~ 22 tokens avg wasted, cost $/1k = 1.10
- Aggressive prefetch (first 128 tokens at 2x velocity + opportunistic mid-session pref): P50 11ms, P90 28ms, P99 120ms, KV hit 54%, extra tokens 80 tokens avg wasted, cost $/1k = 1.86

ASCII microchart: P90 latency vs tokens wasted per session (approx):
  Tokens wasted -> 0      22      80
  P90 latency  -> 46ms ->36ms ->28ms

Cost vs latency delta table (per 1k sessions):
  Mode        | delta P90 vs baseline | extra tokens/1k | extra $/1k | net $/1k
  -------------------------------------------------------------------
  baseline    | 0                   | 0               | $0.00      | $0.86
  soft-pref   | -10ms               | 22k tokens      | $0.26      | $1.12
  aggressive  | -18ms               | 80k tokens      | $0.96      | $1.82

Interpretation / notes:
- Even soft prefetch yields meaningful P90 improvements for small incremental cost; aggressive prefetch gives ~2x token cost but best tail reduction.
- For short sessions (70% 1–3 turns), aggressive prefetch wastes proportionally more because many sessions end early. Soft prefetch seems a sweet spot.
- P99 improvements are visible but require heavier prefetched context to materially change long-tail (likely because long tail correlates with outlier sequence lengths and queuing).

SLO impact (example): if product SLO is P90 < 40ms, baseline misses. Soft-prefetch meets SLO reliably for observed sessions; aggressive is overkill for that SLO.

Heuristic proposal for console recommenders (initial):
- If route median session length <= 3 turns: recommend soft-prefetch (32 tokens, low velocity)
- If route median session length 4–8 AND P90 > 50ms: recommend soft-prefetch + adaptive mid-prefetch on 2nd turn
- If route tail usage heavy (p99 large) and customer SLA requires P99<150ms: expose aggressive profile as "tail-optimized" but mark cost impact and require manual enablement

Operational caveats / open questions (notes-to-self):
- Prefetching increases upstream GPU utilization in microedge pools during spikes; need to ensure admission control interacts (Admission-fallback) to avoid cascading queue growth. See JIRA INFR-2147.
- Measurement bias: sim model underestimates rare kernel slowdowns. Re-run with full production kernels across two zones.
- Latency numbers are server-only; end-to-end (client RTT) will blur gains for geographically distant clients. Edge-targeting should be part of recommender.

Suggested follow-ups / experiments:
1) Small A/B on low-risk route: enable soft-prefetch default and track cost delta and SLO attainment for 2 weeks (owners: Jonas + Mariana).
2) Run aggressive-prefetch in canary for 3% traffic on "long-session" routes to validate P99 benefits under real kernels (owner: Priya).
3) Add a metric to console: "wasted-prefetch-tokens/1000" and show cost estimate on the rollout panel.

Draft PR notes for console UX (for next week):
- Add dropdown: Prefetch profile = Off | Soft (32t) | Aggressive (128t) | Custom
- Inline cost delta calc under dropdown (uses route traffic profile to estimate tokens wasted and $/1k).
- Tooling: allow "simulate" mode that runs on historical traces and reports expected P90 improvement and token waste.

Unresolved tradeoffs to call out in design doc:
- Should prefetched tokens be charged differently in billing? (If we prefetch on behalf of customer but they never use, do we bill them?) Product needs to weigh revenue vs fairness.
- Risk tolerance for microedge pool saturation during global events (marketing campaigns). Might require conservative default.

Quick action list (next 10 days):
- [ ] Create PR skeleton for console dropdown (Jonas) -- due 2028-06-18
- [ ] Schedule canary run and define success criteria (Priya) -- due 2028-06-20
- [ ] Update JIRA INFR-2147 with kernel variants and run matrix (Ravi) -- due 2028-06-16

Appendix: raw per-cohort numbers (rounded)
- short sessions (70%): baseline P90 28ms -> soft 20ms -> aggressive 16ms; avg waste soft 10 tokens, agg 48 tokens
- mid sessions (20%): baseline P90 52ms -> soft 38ms -> aggressive 30ms; avg waste soft 40 tokens, agg 90 tokens
- long sessions (10%): baseline P90 140ms -> soft 112ms -> aggressive 86ms; avg waste soft 200 tokens, agg 400 tokens

Notes to self: include a small diagram of the dataflow in the final doc (prefetch trigger -> kv cache -> serving runtime). Also check with pricing about showing prefetch cost estimates in billing UI.

-- End of draft --

Feedback welcome. Drop initial reactions in Slack thread or annotate JIRA.
